title: US Expands Iranian Maritime Blockade to Ship-to-Ship Transfers, Ukraine Plans to Triple Deep Strikes, and Japan and India Deepen Defense Ties
subhead: Washington tightens its naval blockade of Iran to target ship-to-ship cargo transfers as Houthi missiles strike Riyadh, Ukraine moves to triple long-range deep strikes despite US hesitation, and Japan and India agree to expand defense industrial cooperation.

sections.heading: US Expands Iranian Blockade to Ship-to-Ship Transfers Amid Riyadh Strikes
sections.body:
The United States expanded its maritime blockade of Iranian ports and coastline to cover any vessel receiving cargo via ship-to-ship transfer from ships that loaded in Iran, USNI News reports, citing the Joint Maritime Information Center. Under the tightened enforcement, third-party tankers conducting at-sea transfers of Iranian cargo risk interdiction as Washington seeks to choke off maritime revenue streams.

The move comes as regional hostilities intensify: Al Jazeera reports Houthi missile fire rocked Riyadh's financial center, while The War Zone notes the Pentagon is surging uncrewed systems into CENTCOM waters—including deploying the Regent Squire wing-in-ground-effect drone to patrol the Middle East. Separately, Le Monde writes that the 40-day US air campaign against Iran has yet to achieve White House strategic objectives.
sections.whyItMatters: Extending blockade interdiction to ship-to-ship transfers closes a primary evasion loophole for Iranian exports, raising maritime enforcement tempo across the Gulf and Arabian Sea.

sections.heading: Ukraine Plans to Double Drone Supplies and Triple Deep Strikes
sections.body:
Ukraine is forging ahead with plans to double its drone supplies and triple long-range deep strikes inside Russian-held territory with European backing, Defense News reports, pushing forward even after Washington urged Kyiv to prioritize front-line defense and midrange fires. Satellite imagery reviewed by The War Zone shows impacts from Ukraine's latest Neptune missile strike on the Kerch Bridge, though the rail span has proven harder to sever than the roadway.

Kyiv is also scouring allied inventories for additional Mirage 2000 fighter jets, The War Zone reports, though finding significant airframe numbers quickly remains difficult. Meanwhile, The Independent notes a leading UK military think tank warned the British Army must train nearly half of its infantry to operate drones to remain combat-effective.
sections.whyItMatters: Ukraine's decision to triple deep strikes with European support—even over US reservations—shows Kyiv relying on domestic long-range missiles and drones to sustain leverage against Russian logistics.

sections.heading: US Approved Over 800,000 Nvidia and AMD AI Chips for PLA-Linked Firms
sections.body:
Confidential records released by US lawmakers revealed that the Commerce Department approved exports of more than 800,000 Nvidia and AMD AI chips to Chinese companies—including firms linked to Megaspeed and groups the Pentagon believes are tied to the People's Liberation Army, the New York Times and Financial Times report. The disclosures sharpen scrutiny over Washington's export-control enforcement just as lawmakers debate tighter restrictions on cloud and chip access.

In parallel, Military Times reports a new assessment warning that US missile shortages are creating operational range problems across key theaters, underscoring munitions stockpiling bottlenecks across the US defense industrial base.
sections.whyItMatters: Proof that 800,000 advanced AI chips were cleared for firms tied to China's military is poised to trigger sharper congressional oversight of Commerce Department licensing.

sections.heading: US Navy Floats Foreign-Owned Frigate Yard; Hegseth Forms Autonomous Command
sections.body:
The US Navy's nominee for its number-two civilian post, Bill Toti, told lawmakers Thursday the service wants a new foreign-owned shipyard built inside the United States dedicated to small surface combatants and frigates, USNI News reports. The proposal highlights acute domestic shipyard capacity shortfalls as lawmakers separately moved to trim nearly $20 billion from the Navy's FY2027 shipbuilding request.

On force modernization, USNI News highlights a Congressional Research Service report examining Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's directive establishing an Autonomous Warfare Command to consolidate uncrewed military systems. Meanwhile, The Guardian reports the US Army postponed a controlled detonation of bomb-making chemicals in Iowa following local outcry over lead dust plumes.
sections.whyItMatters: Inviting foreign shipbuilders to finance US frigate yards signals that domestic maritime industrial bottlenecks can no longer be solved solely through traditional US prime contractors.

sections.heading: Japan and India Expand Defense Ties Amid AUKUS Submarine Warnings
sections.body:
Japan and India agreed to expand military and defense industry cooperation, ABC News reports, reinforcing Indo-Pacific security alignment as Tokyo and New Delhi seek resilient co-development and supply partnerships. In Washington, however, The Guardian reports the Congressional Budget Office warned that supplying nuclear-powered submarines to Australia under the AUKUS pact would diminish the US Navy's own attack submarine fleet for 'many years' while raising questions over wartime operational commitments.

Separately, Times of Israel reports US Jewish lawmakers warned that a provision in pending defense legislation allowing chaplains to conduct public worship according to personal beliefs could enable proselytizing in the ranks, while NBC News notes Salvadoran troops in Haiti launched an operation against a prominent gang leader's compound.
sections.whyItMatters: While Japan-India defense cooperation strengthens regional deterrence, CBO warnings on AUKUS submarine transfers expose hard industrial trade-offs inside America's undersea fleet capacity.

bottomLine: Washington is tightening maritime interdiction against Iran and reorganizing around autonomous warfare, yet domestic shipyard bottlenecks, missile shortages, and AUKUS submarine trade-offs reveal real industrial limits. Abroad, Ukraine's push to triple deep strikes and Japan-India defense coordination show allies building independent capacity rather than waiting for US industrial bottlenecks to clear.
sources: USNI News, Al Jazeera, The War Zone, Defense News, New York Times, Financial Times, The Independent, Military Times, ABC News, The Guardian, Times of Israel, NBC News
